decisions.statement: A floor is settled whole before it is played, so play reads it rather than makes it up.
A floor states its number, its name, the read on entering, its exits and its rooms.
A room states what is there to be found, and a second search of it finds nothing better.
A thing a player reliably reaches for is settled here, and a dead end is settled as one.
Water, fire, light, cover, a weapon, a mechanism and every exit are settled that way.
An encounter states what starts it, the whole sheet of what is met, and what is won.
An enemy states the weakness reasoning finds, and the multiplier engaging it carries.
No enemy states a derived stat, every one falling out of the mechanic computing it.
What a floor says to the game master alone is apart from what a player is read.
A floor read twice reads the same, so nothing settled here is settled again in play.
The rows here are what the tower's location and encounter pages were made from.
This property is gone, and a place is a location page whatever game holds it.

definition: the floors a tower game has been climbed through
